settings.title: Bluetooth Mesh options
settings.description: A mesh lamp offers a single Bluetooth proxy connection slot. Keeping it open makes commands instant, but prevents the Häfele Connect Mesh app from connecting to the lamp while this integration is loaded.

data_description.inverted_ctl: Tick a lamp that shows warm white when Home Assistant says cool, and cool when it says warm. Its requested temperature is then mirrored before being sent, from the next command onwards — ticking the box does not re-colour a lamp that is already lit. Leave every other lamp unticked: mirroring a lamp that is already correct inverts warm and cool end to end. This is set per lamp because the quirk varies between models and firmware of the same manufacturer.
data_description.keepalive_seconds: How long to hold the proxy connection after the last command. 0 = always connected (most responsive; the Häfele app cannot use the lamp). A positive value hands the lamp back to the app after that idle time, at the cost of a few seconds to reconnect on the next command. In that mode Home Assistant does not probe the lamp in the background, so as to leave the slot free: a lamp that is switched off at the wall or unplugged keeps showing as available until the next command fails.
data_description.src_addr: The address Home Assistant sends from. 0 derives it automatically, which is almost always right. Set it only if commands are ignored with no error: an export lists no provisioner, so if the vendor app claimed the same address, every message is discarded as a replay and nothing anywhere says so.

add_device.title: Add a device
add_device.description: Devices HA has heard that are factory reset and waiting to be set up, most recently heard first. A battery device (dimmer wheel, switch) only announces itself briefly after it is woken or reset: wake it, then choose "Search again" and Submit. It is the entry seen a few seconds ago. While a device is being added, keep pressing it: the wheel or switch, or the dimmer's button (power or R).

data_description.name: What the device is called in Home Assistant

pair_switch.title: Pair a wheel / switch
pair_switch.description: The dimmer stores the pairing and reacts to the wheel directly, without Home Assistant. Pair one wheel to several dimmers by running this once per dimmer.

remove_device.title: Remove a device
remove_device.description: The device is factory reset over the mesh (as when removing it in the SG app) and removed from Home Assistant. A wheel or switch is unpaired from every dimmer first. A battery device sleeps: press or turn it while it is being removed.

data.force: Remove anyway if the device does not answer

progress.adding: Setting up {name}: provisioning, then configuring. This takes up to two minutes. Keep pressing the device while it runs: the wheel or switch, or the dimmer's button (power or R).
progress.removing: Resetting {name}. For a battery device, keep pressing or turning it. This takes up to a minute.

error.no_devices: No device waiting to be set up was found. Factory reset the device (SG: the reset procedure in its manual), make sure it is near a Bluetooth proxy, then press Submit to search again.
error.send_failed: The command could not be sent: is the mesh connected?

abort.backup_written: The network (keys, nodes and device keys) was written to {path}. Keep a copy somewhere safe: without it every device must be factory reset if this Home Assistant is lost. It can be imported again with Reconfigure.
abort.device_added_switch: {name} was added as {unicast}. Its button and battery entities appear once it is used. Pair it to a dimmer with the bluetooth_mesh.pair_switch action.
abort.device_added_unconfigured: {name} was provisioned as {unicast} but did not answer the configuration ({error}). Its keys are saved. Wake it (press or turn it) and run the bluetooth_mesh.configure_node action for {unicast}.
abort.add_device_failed: The device could not be added: {error}. It is not part of the network; factory reset it and try again.
abort.not_loaded: The integration must be running (connected to the mesh) to add a device.
abort.paired: {switch} now controls {node}. Try it: it works without Home Assistant.
abort.nothing_to_pair: Add at least one SG dimmer and one wheel or switch first.
abort.device_removed: {name} was factory reset and removed. It can be added again, here or in the SG app.
abort.device_forgotten: {name} was removed from Home Assistant, but did not confirm the reset. Factory reset it by hand before using it again.
abort.nothing_to_remove: There is no device to remove.

proxy_unreachable.title: No Bluetooth proxy for mesh network {network}

proxy_stuck.title: Restart the Bluetooth proxy {proxy}
proxy_stuck.description:
The proxy **{proxy}** (`{proxy_address}`) has refused every connection to the mesh network “{network}” {failures} times in a row, each time within about a second, while it still hears the node. The lamp is not the problem: the proxy itself is stuck on this address, and only restarting it clears the condition.

Cut the power to **{proxy}** for a few seconds, then plug it back in. If your own ESPHome configuration gives it a *Restart* button, that works too. **Do not press *Factory reset***: it does not clear this condition, and it can erase the Wi-Fi settings the proxy was set up with. Home Assistant reconnects on its own within seconds of the proxy coming back, and this issue disappears.

The condition appears when the node disappears (unplugged, out of range) while the proxy is holding a connection to it. Nothing in this integration can clear it from the Home Assistant side.
